questions.prompt: n = 8, Σx = 44, Σy = 123, Σx² = 284, Σy² = 2003, Σxy = 744. Compute r (3 decimals).
questions.explain: Num: 744 − 44×123/8 = 67.5. Den: √[(284 − 242)(2003 − 1891.125)] = √(42 × 111.875) = 68.547. **r = 0.985** — very strong positive: higher ad spend ↔ higher sales (no causation claim!).

options: Strong NEGATIVE linear relationship — as x rises, y tends to fall
85% of y is explained by x
questions.explain: Sign = direction, magnitude = strength: |r| ≈ 0.85 is strong. The '% explained' is **r² = 0.7225 (72.25%)**, not r; and the slope b₁ has different units entirely.

questions.prompt: n = 6 ranked items, Σd² = 8. Compute r_s (3 decimals).
x̄ = 6.286, ȳ = 4.929, b₁ = 0.367. Compute b₀ = ȳ − b₁x̄ (3 decimals).
questions.explain: b₀ = 4.929 − 0.367×6.286 = 4.929 − 2.304 = **2.625**. The least-squares line ALWAYS passes through (x̄, ȳ) — that's why this formula works.

questions.prompt: In ŷ = 2.625 + 0.367x (salary in RM-thousands vs years of experience), b₁ = 0.367 means:
options: Each additional year of experience is associated with ≈ RM367/month more salary
questions.explain: **Slope = change in ŷ per unit change in x.** Intercept b₀ = 2.625 = baseline at x = 0 (entry-level ≈ RM2,625). The interpretation marks demand units + direction.
SSR = 200 − 38 = 162; **R² = 162/200 = 0.81** → '81% of the variation in y is explained by the variation in x.'

questions.prompt: The exam's regression question typically asks, in order:
options: Sums table → r (+ strength sentence) → b₁, b₀ → line ŷ = b₀ + b₁x → predict ŷ(x₀) inside the range → R² or slope t-test
Slope first, then r, then sums
questions.explain: Q4 (Pearson + interpretation) feeds Q5 (line + prediction + R²/slope test) — the SAME sums (Σx, Σy, Σx², Σy², Σxy) power everything. Compute them once, carefully, with a table.
